question.leadin: Three prominent figures with this last name were assassinated by political and/or religious opponents inthe twentieth century.
question.text: Give this shared surname of several figures in Indian political history, including Prime Minister Rajiv andindependence leader Mahatma.
question.clue: Another leader with this surname resolved some tension with a western neighbor in the 1972 Shimla Agreement and was opposed by the Janata Party.

swap.text: Srivijaya's capital was sacked in the 11th century by the Chola dynasty, which followed this religion. Srivijaya was named based on this religion's sacred language of Sanskrit.
swap.clue: In September 2015, 27 people were killed by a bomb at the Erawan shrine, a worship place of this religion in Thailand.

question.leadin: This country became the first Muslim-majority democracy to be led by a woman when Benazir Bhutto led the PPP to victory in 1988 elections.
question.text: Name this country where Bhutto was assassinated in 2007 at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi.
question.clue: At a 2007 rally, a female leader of this country and daughter of former leader Zulfikar Ali was assassinated at a political rally in Rawalpindi.

swap.text: A notable example of Mughul architecture is this white-domed mausoleum in Agra, built by Akbar's grandson Shah Jahan for his wife.
swap.clue: A Moonlight garden is across the river from this building, and this structure is surrounded by red sandstone on three sides.

question.leadin: The last emperor of this empire was a noted Urdu poet named Bahadur Shah II.
question.text: Name this Indian Empire, whose ruler Akbar won the 1556 Battle of Panipat and abolished the jizya tax.
question.clue: The founder of this empire won the Battle of Panipat.

swap.leadin: This Seven Years' War battle helped destroy French influence in India.
swap.text: Name this battle which saw British forces supporting the Bengalese pretender Mir Jafar rout Nawab Siraj-ud-daula's army despite being outnumbered seventeen to one.
swap.clue: It took place a year after the death of the beloved Alivardi Khan, whose nephew was killed by the son of the perfidious Mir Jafar following it.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the cartoons of Thomas Nast.
question.text: In order to attack Catholicism, Nast depicted an upside-down American flag, ruins of a public school, poor, defenseless protestant schoolchildren, and crocodiles with bishop hats for snouts on the banks of an "American" version of this river.
question.clue: The iron-rich Magadha kingdom along this river's banks gave birth to a dynasty ruled by Nanda.

swap.text: This large city was the headquarters of the English East India Company after 1773. Situated on the Ganges delta, this city saw Britishers imprisoned by the Nawab of Bengal in its namesake "Black Hole", and the battle of Plassey was fought north of it.

question.text: In this city, a "pact" between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League committed both to opposing the British Raj. Colin Campbell relieved a pre-Raj siege of this city during the Sepoy mutiny.
question.clue: This city's British Residency was besieged for several months in 1857.

swap.text: da Gama paved the way for Portugal to obtain this small state in western India, which remained under Portuguese control until the 1960s.
swap.clue: Much later, this state became part of a union territory along with the exclaves of Daman and Diu on the coast.

question.leadin: One of these things in Lumbini described how a ruler visited the city 20 years into his reign and abolished taxes there.
question.text: Name this collection of over thirty inscriptions that encourage right behavior and kindness towards animals and others. These inscriptions were created in response to the violence of the Kalinga War.
question.answerHtml: edicts of Ashoka [accept pillar edicts of Ashoka, accept rock edicts of Ashoka, accept pillars of Ashoka, accept pillars of Dharma, prompt on partial answers]
question.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about amendments to Pakistan's constitution.
swap.text: The first and second amendments to Pakistan's constitution were passed under Zulfikar Ali, a member of this prominent Pakistani political dynasty which runs the Pakistan People's Party.
swap.clue: One member of this family famously stated that his government would "eat grass" if it would help obtain nuclear weapons.

question.text: The regulations were partially prompted by the company's increased power after it seized a series of Diwani rights to this region after the battles of Buxar and Plassey.
question.clue: This region widely cultivated phuti cotton to export fine Mal-Mal muslin.

swap.leadin: A musical automaton of a tiger mauling a European man was discovered in this ruler's capital after its capture by the British.
swap.text: Name this "Tiger of Mysore" who, along with his father, resisted the British East India Company in four wars. His defeat at the Battle of Seringapatam ended Mysore's independence.
swap.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

question.leadin: One long term cause of this conflict was the Doctrine of Lapse, in which any state without an heir under the influence of the British East India Company was annexed to it.
question.text: Name this rebellion which caused many warlords to proclaim Bahadur Shah II Emperor of India.
question.answerHtml: Sepoy Rebellion [or Indian Mutiny of 1857; or Indian Rebellion of 1857; accept equivalents]
question.clue: This event began after Mangal Pandey was hanged for attacking two officers.

swap.text: Fellow revolutionary Udham Singh spent 30 years planning to assassinate Michael O'Dwyer for his role in this massacre carried out by British officer Reginald Dyer.
swap.clue: The chief perpetrator claimed that it was in response to an attack on Marcia Sherwood, and had the support of Police Superintendent Ploper.

question.leadin: This empire's power was broken after its forces, convinced that a British cavalry escort for an ammunition resupply was a flanking maneuver, retreated at the Battle of Ferozeshah (feh-roh-zay-shah).
question.text: Name this major power in the Punjab in the early 19th century, which clashed with forces of the British East India Company in two namesake wars in the 1840s. This highly militaristic empire was founded by Ranjit.
question.clue: Victories at the battles of Attock and Jamrud, among others, brought this empire to its westernmost extent at the expense of the Durrani Empire.

swap.leadin: They were named for named for a kingdom in southern India ruled by the Wodeyar dynasty.
swap.text: Name this series of four wars ending in 1799. At the end, the British defeated Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan and annexed much of their land.
swap.clue: The second, which lasted from 1780-17884, was ended by the Treaty of Mangalore, and saw the defeat of Hyder Ali at Porto Nova and his subsequent death, leaving his kingdom to his son Tipu Sultan, who fought against Cornwallis.

question.text: The Mysorean ruler Hyder Ali reprimanded his admiral, Ali Raja, for blinding the sultan of this place. Operation Cactus intervened in a much later coup attempt in this territory.
question.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

swap.leadin: Charles Boone commissioned a "floating castle" ship to defeat this empire's naval officer Kanhoji Angre, but failed when that ship, the HMS Phram, caught fire.
swap.text: Name this empire primarily ruled by a peshwa. This empire's first chhatrapati ("CHUH-truh-puh-tee") established its first capital at Raigad.
swap.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.
